subject: design-technology
title: Iterative Design Process
welcome_lead: Spotting needs and writing precise design requirements.
meta_desc: KS3 D&T: research types, course writing.
final_note: A clear spec stops you wandering off-target.

walkthroughs.body_html: Primary research means YOU collect data — surveys, interviews, observing. Secondary means using existing data — websites, books, magazines. Use both.
A specification turns the brief into hard requirements. 'Must hold 1.5 kg', 'Must fit in a 30 cm box', 'Must cost under £10'. Be specific or you can't tell if you've succeeded.
Specification points should be SMART — Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Realistic, Time-bound. 'Looks good' isn't SMART; 'matches 3 user colours' is.

mcqs.q: What force does a rope in a tug-of-war experience?
options: Compression - because it is squeezed by hands.
Tension - it is being pulled at both ends.

mcqs.q: If voltage is doubled and resistance is unchanged, what happens to the current?
options: Current doubles (V = IR, so I = V/R).
